When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 1/10: price-based stress signals absent, realized tape calm vs VIX Spike Tier 4/4 EXTREME, 85% probability, skew plus backwardation plus adaptive all confirmed active simultaneously
Price has not broken; the options market is pricing a break. Trust the VIX Spike read: skew, backwardation, and adaptive signals firing together is a rare alignment that typically leads price deterioration rather than trailing it. The Crash Index measures what has already happened; the VIX tier measures what options traders are paying to hedge against.
Today's tension
The VIX Spike Detector and the Crash Index are telling opposite stories; the options market is the one priced for catastrophe.
Bull
The Crash Index at **1/10** shows no realized stress across equities, credit, or cross-asset relationships. The contrarian score of **40** (ACCUMULATE partial) confirms the broad market has not priced in catastrophe, leaving room for relief.
Bear
The VIX Spike Detector is at Tier **4/4** (EXTREME) with **85%** probability, all three sub-signals confirmed: skew, backwardation, and adaptive. **67.44%** of the **43** cross-asset pairs tracked are diverging bearishly, with **26** bearish pairs against only **3** bullish.
The tell: Whether HYG rolls over while VIX backwardation holds and activates the credit-plus-backwardation confluence, or the Crash Index climbs toward 4 as price action starts confirming what the options market already believes.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The regime sits at 35 (STABLE) with a MIXED bias, the Crash Index at 1/10, and the contrarian score at 40 (ACCUMULATE partial). Three realized-price indicators say nothing has broken yet. Against that, the VIX Spike Detector is at Tier 4/4 with 85% probability and all three sub-signals active, while the divergence composite shows 26 bearish pairs against 3 bullish across 43 tracked relationships. The macro regime reads CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence. That combination presents two frames simultaneously: the realized market says hold, and the options market says hedge.

The CONCENTRATION regime at 55% tells you where the gains are hiding. NDX is up +4.7% over five days while DJI is down -0.7%. A narrow group of stocks is carrying the index and masking the broad internal deterioration that 67.44% divergence confirms. Passive beta is not working here. If you want exposure, you are targeting the specific stocks inside the winning pocket, not the full index.

The stance flips when any of the three stress confluences activate. All three are inactive today: no credit stress pairing with VIX backwardation, no small-cap drawdown, no yen safe-haven flow. That absence is the single reason the Crash Index stays at 1/10 despite everything else. HYG is the primary watch item. If it cracks while VIX backwardation holds, confluence one fires and the calm in the crash score ends.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence means the market's returns are piling into a narrow group of leaders while most of the broad market stagnates or falls. The 55% is moderate conviction, not high.

NDX at +4.7% versus DJI at -0.7% over five days gives you the live version in price: tech mega-cap is doing all the work. In a concentration regime, owning the full index means subsidizing the laggards with the winners' gains.

The divergence composite, with 26 bearish pairs running across 43 relationships, confirms that breadth is not participating in the tech-led move. The regime breaks either toward a broader recovery where rotation bids up cyclicals, or toward a sharper selloff where even the leaders give up their gains.

At 55% confidence, both exits are live.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence here means assets that historically moved together are now moving apart. When QQQ and SPY have a correlation that drifts from +0.75 to -0.38, two instruments that were nearly synchronized have decoupled.

67.44% of the 43 pairs tracked are showing this kind of drift today, with 26 running bearishly and only 3 bullish. The composite sits in the TOPPING zone (the configuration associated with a market preparing to turn lower), with a net bearish bias of 23.

The sharpest breaks: KRE has broken from XLF (regional banks from broad financials), correlation drifting from +0.17 to -0.60, signaling stress localized in smaller banks. Bond volatility (MOVE) decoupled from equity volatility (VIX), drifting from +0.52 to -0.08; the two stress gauges are no longer moving together.

USMV flipped from moving inversely to SPY (correlation -0.91) to moving with it (+0.15), meaning low-volatility stocks have stopped acting as a safe haven. When this many pairs break from historical relationships simultaneously, the broad market's calm surface is covering structural deterioration that has not yet shown up in price.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

The five-day tape has one dominant print: NDX at +4.7% is the strongest reading across the entire cross-region scan while DJI is down -0.7%. That internal US split confirms the CONCENTRATION regime read directly.

Crypto adds the secondary risk-on signal: SOL up +20.2%, BTC up +13.4%. High-beta and momentum-driven assets are leading; defensives are not.

Europe is trailing with STOXX50E down -1.4% against a nearly flat Swiss market at +0.1%. Asia is split, Nikkei up +1.6% while KOSPI is down -0.2%.

The pattern is consistent across every region: narrow leadership in high-growth, tech-adjacent assets and underperformance in cyclicals and old economy exposure. If the concentration cracks in the US session, there is nothing in the cross-region tape showing a rotation bid positioned to catch it.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1/10 and the VIX Spike Detector at Tier 4/4 are reading different things, which is why they coexist coherently. The Crash Index scores realized stress: how much has actually broken across price, credit, and cross-asset behavior.

At 1, almost nothing has broken yet. The VIX Spike Detector reads forward expectation in the options market: with skew, backwardation, and adaptive all confirmed and 85% probability active, options traders are paying up aggressively for tail protection on something they believe is coming.

These two readings often coexist in the early phase of a vol event. Options lead; price follows.

Treat the Crash Index as your current location and the VIX tier as the probability map for where you are heading.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Each tier indicates a historical probability of VIX +50% at 60d (cycle backtest 2023-2026, vs baseline 37%). Strict sizing: tier 2 = 1-2% book hedges, tier 3 = 3-5% long-vol, tier 4 = 5-10% MAX (rare confluence).

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.

Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
